create.name: Banqi: Level 7 versus Level 8, annotated
create.description: A recorded engine game, analyzed with the served Level 8 engine and pinned net. Flip choices use public pool means; reveal luck is separate. From mistboard.com/rules/banqi.

children.text: The red advisor moves from b3 to b4 and removes the last black soldier. Level 7 now has no legal move, so Level 8 wins by stalemate. The result follows from the board, not from a resignation or a clock.

comments.text: The red soldier on c4 captures the black general on b4. This is Banqi’s rank exception: a soldier can capture a general. The highest-ranked piece still needs protection from the lowest-ranked enemy.

The black general moves from d4 to c4. Level 8’s analysis prefers d4 to e4 instead; the first-seat estimate falls from 96.2% to 64.5% after the played move. The side line shows that legal alternative without turning over a new tile.

The flip on g4 reveals the red general, a piece belonging to Level 8. That still helps Level 7 in this position: its public-pool expectation is 34.2%, while this particular reveal gives 44.8%. A piece of the opponent’s ink can be a lucky draw because its location matters.

The red elephant from a4 captures that black cannon on b4. In Banqi an elephant can capture a cannon by rank. Level 8 trades back using an already revealed piece, without spending a turn on another flip.

The black cannon on b2 jumps over the covered b3 tile to capture the red advisor on b4. A cannon needs exactly one screen; that screen can stay covered, so this capture gives neither player its identity.

The opening flip reveals a black cannon on b2. Level 7 therefore takes black ink and Level 8 takes red ink. The flip has a 48.1% public-pool expectation for Level 7; this cannon produces 44.0%. The difference is reveal luck, not a mistake in choosing the square.

Level 7 has the first seat and black ink; Level 8 has the second seat and red ink. The graph is from the first seat. Flip grades compare public pool means, while the die marks the revealed piece’s luck.
